question.prompt: A circle has center \((-10, -4)\) and radius \(13.\) Another circle has center \((3, 9)\) and radius \(\sqrt{65}.\) The line passing through the two points of intersection of the two circles has equation \(x + y = c.\) What is \(c?\)

solutions.title: Subtract the circle equations
solutions.explanation:
Each intersection point satisfies both circle equations. Subtracting those equations will cancel the squared terms and leave a line.

The equations are
\[
(x+10)^2+(y+4)^2=169
\]
and
\[
(x-3)^2+(y-9)^2=65.
\]
Expanding and moving the constants to the right gives
\[
x^2+y^2+20x+8y=53,
\]
\[
x^2+y^2-6x-18y=-25.
\]
Subtracting the second equation from the first yields
\[
26x+26y=78,
\qquad x+y=3.
\]
Both intersection points lie on this line, so it is the line through them. Hence \(\boxed{c=3}\), choice A.
